accuracy.evidence: Checked against the English National Curriculum (2013) Year 1 writing composition (re-read what they have written to check that it makes sense; discuss what they have written with the teacher or other pupils) and Year 2 (make simple additions, revisions and corrections; evaluate writing with the teacher and other pupils; expanded noun phrases; subordination using because), and CCSS W.K.5 / W.1.5 (respond to questions and suggestions from peers and add details to strengthen writing). Every lab answer is grammatical and every distractor is labelled with the question it does answer (where, when, who, how much).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented early-revision slips: reading what you meant instead of what you wrote (missing word; a wrong gap is read back so the child hears it), adding any detail rather than one that answers the reader's question (at the park for 'what did it look like?', on Sunday for 'where?'), circular reasons ('because I was happy'), hearing a wish as criticism, copying the question into the writing, and starting again instead of adding.

lab_distinct.evidence: Built around responding to a reader: a sticky question drives every insertion, the because-step answers 'why?', a star/wish sorter treats feedback as a job, and a before/after story maps each new detail to the question it answers. Checking Your Own Work (flagcheck) is about recounting and checking sums, Writing Process Vocabulary (flagwproc) orders process steps, and Reviewing your own writing (flagrvw) is for older writers judging effect; the shingle gate passed against all flag_*.js files.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child hears a missing word by reading back, learns that a detail must match the question (each wrong card names the question it answers instead), adds reasons with the conjunction because, reframes a wish as a job, and then sees all five answered questions together in Sam's revised story. This is the topic's evidence list: spot a missing word, add a detail in response to a question, make an improvement from feedback.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong options: 'Yes, it is fine' for 'We went the park' (disproved by reading it back), 'It was fun' as the answer to 'Where did you go?' (disproved by the where/when feedback), and 'Yes, it is bad' for a wish (disproved in the sorter, which calls a wish a job).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Four rotating revise-this-sentence questions with seven distinct m= messages: off-question detail, not re-reading (a cat cat), ignoring the feedback, circular reason, copying the question, rubbing everything out, and the correct answer explained.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs are short read-aloud sentences using concrete examples (big and spotty, by the river) within the family kid limit; lab prompts are one line. Adult text names the curriculum terms re-read, detail, adjective, conjunction, expanded noun phrase and because within the adult limit.

no_filler.evidence: Passed the filler regex and the 12% duplicate gate. Each kid sentence carries one instruction; adult paragraphs cover curriculum placement, the two key skills and their common slips, the vocabulary to model, and what the lab does.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px Android and iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark: the first pass squashed three long answer cards into one row, so they were restacked as full-width rows and the page box was shortened; star/wish bins were split into a big title and a short line so nothing clips. Buttons use the young-learner size.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs: every task completes with Show me on desktop and iPhone 13, the challenge shows, axe WCAG 2.1 AA is clean in both themes, no console errors. Every drag has a button route (gap buttons naming the two words either side, one button per detail card, Star / Wish buttons, one button per new detail) and the canvas aria-label reports each read-back.

sources: Department for Education (2013), The national curriculum in England: English programmes of study, Year 1 and Year 2 writing composition, and Appendix 2 vocabulary, grammar and punctuation (expanded noun phrases; subordination using because)
Common Core State Standards for English Language Arts, W.K.5 and W.1.5 (with guidance and support from adults, respond to questions and suggestions from peers and add details to strengthen writing)
Education Endowment Foundation (2020), Improving Literacy in Key Stage 1: teach pupils to plan, draft, revise and edit, with adult feedback during writing
